 Order

The petitioner is the 1st accused in CC No.421/2024 on the file of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-II, Hosdurg, which has originated from Crime No.208/2022 registered by the Chittarikal Police Station, Kasaragod, alleging the commission of the offences punishable under Sections 419 and 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal code.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The crux of prosecution case is that:
The accused 1 and 2, with an intention to cheat, established an entity named 'Span Associates' using the Aadhaar card of the 2nd accused.
They advertised job visas for Singapore in areas such as Cherupuzha, Kannur to attract victims.
Within the association, the 1st accused impersonated the 2nd accused with the consent of the latter.
On 07.03.2020, they collected a total amount of 1,77,500 from CW1 by promising a Singapore visa.
However, the accused neither CRL.MC NO. 9802 OF 2025 2026:KER:9638 provided the visa nor refunded the amount, thereby committed the alleged offences.
3. I have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
4. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is totally innocent in the above crime.

Even if the allegations in Annexures A1 FIR and A2 final report are taken on their face value,
the same would not constitute the offences alleged against the petitioner.
The entire allegation is against the 2nd accused.
Therefore, even if the petitioner withstands the trial, it will not lead to conviction of the petitioner.
Hence, the entire proceedings as against the petitioner may be quashed.
5. The learned Public Prosecutor seriously opposes the Crl.M.C.
She submits that the petitioner is a habitual offender.

He is involved in four crimes of similar nature registered by the Pathanamthitta,
Karukachal, Thamarassery and Pulpally Police Stations.

There are specific overt acts attributed Prasad.N vs State Of Kerala on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79665201/
2 against the petitioner, which establishes his culpability in the crime.
This Court may not embark upon a mini-trial and come CRL.MC NO. 9802 OF 2025 2026:KER:9638 to a conclusion that the petitioner has not committed the above offences.
The Crl.M.C. is devoid of merit and may be dismissed.
6. The essence of the prosecution case is that, the petitioner along with the 2nd accused, in furtherance of their common intention had cheated the defacto complainant.
On going through the final report, I find that the prosecution has cited ten witnesses and placed reliance on their statements.
The materials also produced along with the final report prima facie establishes the petitioner's culpability in the crime.

7. It is well-settled that this Court has broad plenary powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which corresponds to Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023, to quash criminal proceedings.
However, such inherent power, though expansive in nature, is not unbridled or unlimited.
They are to be exercised sparingly, with circumspection, and within the parameters delineated by judicial precedents.

One of the elementary principles to quash a criminal proceeding is that, even if allegations in the first information report or the complaint are taken at their face CRL.MC NO. 9802 OF 2025 2026:KER:9638 value and accepted in their entirety, the same will not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

(Read the decisions in State of Haryana and others v. Bhajan Lal and others [(1992) Supp (1) SCC 335],
Central Bureau of Investigation v. Aryan Singh and Others [(2023) 18 SCC 399], Daxaben v. State of Gujarat and Others [(2022) 16 SCC 117] and Monica Kumar and Another v. State of U.P. and Others [(2008) 8 SCC 781]).
8.

The scope of enquiry is confined to whether, on a plain reading of the FIR/complaint and accompanying material, the ingredients of the alleged offence are disclosed.

sentences.text: On an analysis of the allegations in the FIR and the final report, I am not satisfied that this is a fit case to exercise CRL.MC NO. 9802 OF 2025 2026:KER:9638 the inherent powers of this Court under Section 528 of the BNSS, since the allegations are taken on their face value it would constitute the offence.
Furthermore, I find that the petitioner has criminal antecedents, since he is involved in four other crimes of similar nature.

In the aforesaid circumstances, I dismiss the Crl.M.C., but by reserving the right of the petitioner to raise all his contentions before the Trial Court, including filing an application for discharge, if the charge is not framed till date.
If such application is filed, the Trial Court is directed to consider and dispose the application, untrammelled by any observations made in this order.
